correctness.summary: The half-disk upper bound is proved exactly on the circular arc and vertical chord and extended by the maximum-modulus principle. A convex two-point subgradient certificate proves the matching lower bound, with a fixed 3x3 real-normal sharp matrix. The unequal extragradient parameters reproduce the minimax polynomial, and the common-step benchmark has a separate endpoint-and-boundary proof. Deterministic numerical checks agree to floating-point precision.

limitations: Affine real normal operators only for the Euclidean contraction statement.
Exact arithmetic and known positive parameters mu and L.
One stationary degree-two cycle; no long-horizon optimality claim.
No claim for nonnormal, projected, nonlinear, adaptive, momentum, or higher-degree methods.
Older complex Chebyshev and semi-iterative literature leaves residual historical-equivalence uncertainty.
Independent audit has not been performed.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The general complex Chebyshev/minimax framework is classical and explicitly credited. Checked modern work uses the same strongly-monotone half-disk but does not state the exact degree-two closed form, unequal-step extragradient realization, or optimized common-step factor. Manteuffel 1982 and older semi-iterative literature are the principal historical-equivalence risk because complete theorem-level coverage was not available for every source.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result gives a sharp closed-form robust two-evaluation design on a natural normal strongly-monotone class, identifies a fixed low-dimensional hard instance, and quantifies exactly the loss from forcing classical extragradient to use one common step.
